subject: Portable pull-request and diff review discipline for evaluating proposed code before merge: intent/scope validation,…

evals.prompt: Define code-review in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the code-review skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind code-review. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "fix this bug that production users are reporting". Should code-review activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force code-review onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to test-coverage-strategy, testing-strategy, naming-conventions, owasp-security, diff-analysis, refactor, debugging, evaluation.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "review this PR for correctness and project conventions". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying code-review.

Place code-review among its adjacent skills (test-coverage-strategy, testing-strategy, naming-conventions, owasp-security, diff-analysis, refactor, debugging, evaluation). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about code-review and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
